info.title: uapi
info.description:
Native HTTP REST API for OpenWrt. Translates standard REST verbs into ubus/uci operations so edge routers become first-class targets for Infrastructure-as-Code workflows.

## Quickstart

Mint a token on the router (one-time):

```sh
uapi-token create --name terraform_prod --scope '*:rw' --expires-in 90d
```

Then call the API:

```sh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://router/api/v4/firewall/rules
```

## Two surfaces

- **Curated resources** under `/api/v4/<domain>/...` - hand-written schemas, stable across the major. Field names are `snake_case`; uci booleans normalize to JSON booleans; uci list options surface as JSON arrays.
- **Raw passthrough** under `/api/v4/raw/<package>/<id>` - generic uci access for the long tail. Same atomic-transaction recipe and same auth model, but payloads follow uci's field names directly (and move when upstream OpenWrt does).

## Resource shape

Every curated resource carries `id` (the uci section name) and `managed: bool` at the top level. `managed` is false for an anonymous section, whose name libuci derives from its position in the file at each load, until `POST /<resource>/<id>/adopt` renames it to a stable one. Server-derived state lives under `runtime: {...}`: it is read-only and never part of the desired state or of a plan diff. Where it shows what a daemon or the kernel holds beside what uci holds, a client can report the difference.

## Auth

Bearer tokens with hierarchical scopes (e.g. `firewall:rules:rw`, `*:ro`). See the **Auth / Tokens** group for mint/list/revoke and the `/uapi/whoami` endpoint for introspection.

## Optimistic concurrency

Every curated-resource GET and write returns an `ETag` header that is a stable hash of the resource's own body (the `runtime` block is excluded so live ubus state never trips a 412). Honor with `If-Match` on writes (or the `?if_match=<etag>` query param). `If-None-Match` is honoured on writes too, per RFC 9110 13.1.2: a match, or `*` against an existing resource, gives 412. Preconditions are evaluated before the transaction, so a 412 never leaves a partial write. Conditional GET via `If-None-Match` returns 304 when matching, and the 304 carries the same `ETag`. Raw passthrough, the non-uci endpoints and the read-only lease views carry no `ETag` and so support neither conditional GET nor `If-Match`. Sibling sections in the same package do not influence each other's ETags; If-Match fires only when *this* resource has actually changed.

## Idempotency

`Idempotency-Key` on POST caches the response for 24 h; a repeat with the same key replays. Same key with a different body returns `409 idempotency_key_conflict`.

A client that cannot set a header can pass `?idempotency_key=` instead. In the same way, `?if_match=`, `?if_none_match=` and `?request_id=` stand in for `If-Match`, `If-None-Match` and `X-Request-Id`. A header that is not empty wins over its query form, and an `X-Request-Id` header only when it matches the pattern of `?request_id=`. Each query form is declared on the operations that honour it.

## Sensitive fields (write-only + `has_<field>` presence flag)

Fields holding secret material (passphrases, private keys, PSKs, PKCS#12 paths) are write-only on the wire: GET responses omit the value and surface a read-only `has_<field>: bool` companion indicating presence. Examples: `wireless.interfaces.key`/`has_key`, `network.interfaces.private_key`/`has_private_key`, `network.wireguard_peers.preshared_key`/`has_preshared_key`, `network.interfaces.key`/`has_key` on proto openvpn, and `network.interfaces.password`/`has_password` on proto pppoe, ppp, wwan and openvpn. PATCH that omits a sensitive field carries the existing value forward; rotation is explicit.

## Atomicity

Every write is one transaction: validate, stage, snapshot, commit, reload, restore-on-failure. A write that leaves uci as it was commits and reloads nothing.  `POST /uapi/batch` extends this across N packages under one combined snapshot/restore.

## IMPORTANT - Success != runtime convergence

A 2xx response means that the reload action of each init script that ran **exited 0**, and `X-Reload-Status: no_reload` says that none ran, because the write changed nothing in uci, or because procd runs none of the daemons that read a `dhcp` write. It does NOT mean the daemon has finished re-converging (`network/interfaces` is the dangerous one: a bad change can drop the management link, and the API has already reported success). The `X-Reload-Status` response header surfaces the reload outcome explicitly:

- `X-Reload-Status: ok` - init script ran and exited 0 (not a convergence promise)
- `X-Reload-Status: no_reload` - no init script ran, because the write changed nothing in uci or no daemon that reads it runs
- `X-Reload-Status: unverified` - the write kept its commit, and whether its daemons take the new config is unknown: an init script was still running when uapi stopped waiting for the reloads, 20 s after the first started, or the `dnsmasq --test` check after a dhcp write did not finish within 10 s
- `X-Reload-Status: stopped` - the write kept its commit, but a daemon that it reloaded is down and procd will not start it again on its own, and `X-Reload-Stopped` names it. Only dnsmasq meets it today, after uapi stopped and started it once in the request. `POST /uapi/services/dnsmasq/recover` starts it again

For high-stakes writes (management interface, firewall defaults, uhttpd itself) verify convergence out-of-band. See [`docs/operations.md`](https://github.com/openwrt-iac/uapi/blob/main/docs/operations.md) `Success != converged` for the full contract.

## Compatibility & versioning

A given uapi installation serves exactly one API major. Within a major, additions are backwards-compatible: new endpoints, new optional fields, new error codes, new scopes. Breaking changes require the next major, apart from the carve-outs that docs/versioning.md lists. Operators who need an older major keep that package version installed.

## Schema annotations

Property schemas under `components.schemas.*.properties` carry two annotations beyond the standard OpenAPI shape:

- **`default`**: the value uapi's `fromUci` synthesizes when the underlying uci option is absent. Standard OpenAPI 3.1 / JSON Schema 2020-12 keyword. The framework does NOT apply this default to incoming requests; it is documentation of the server-side fallback so IaC clients can keep the field sticky (Optional+Computed) instead of mistakenly treating it as caller-owned.
- **`x-uapi-clear-on-omit`** (vendor extension, boolean): when present and `true`, the field is caller-owned and an IaC client (e.g. the terraform-provider-uapi) can safely send an explicit JSON null on `PUT`/`PATCH` to clear the underlying uci option. Absence of this flag means the field should be treated as sticky. A field with `default:` MUST NOT carry this flag, and vice versa (the framework's `lint-defaults` enforces this).

## More

- **GitHub:** https://github.com/openwrt-iac/uapi

- **APK feed install:** [/install/](../install/)

tags.name: Firewall / Rules
tags.description: Firewall rules (`config rule`): nested `match` block for src/dest zone, IPs, ports, proto, family, mark, dscp, plus the MARK and DSCP targets and their `set_*` values. Cross-refs `firewall/zones`.

tags.name: Firewall / Redirects
tags.description: Port forwards and NAT loopback (`config redirect`). Cross-refs `firewall/zones`.

tags.name: Firewall / Nat
tags.description: Source NAT (`config nat`): SNAT, MASQUERADE, or exemption from address rewriting, keyed on the outbound zone. Cross-refs `firewall/zones`.

tags.name: Firewall / Forwardings
tags.description: Zone-to-zone forwarding (`config forwarding`).

tags.name: Firewall / Defaults
tags.description: Global firewall defaults singleton: verdicts, syn_flood, tcp_syncookies, flow_offloading.

tags.name: Network / Interfaces
tags.description: Network interfaces (`config interface`). proto static/dhcp/dhcpv6/pppoe/wireguard/etc. `runtime` carries ubus state.

tags.name: Network / Devices
tags.description: Network devices (`config device`): bridges, VLAN (8021q/8021ad), macvlan, veth, tun/tap.

tags.name: Network / Routes
tags.description: Static routes (`config route`).

tags.name: Network / Rules
tags.description: Policy routing rules (`config rule`).

tags.name: Network / Bridge Vlans
tags.description: Bridge VLAN tagging (`config bridge-vlan`).

tags.name: Network / Wireguard Peers
tags.description: WireGuard peers (dynamic uci type `wireguard_<iface>`); preshared_key write-only. `runtime` carries what the kernel holds for the peer, from `wg show`.

tags.name: Network / Wireguard Kernel Peers
tags.description: Read-only collection of the WireGuard peers the kernel holds that no uci section claims, from `wg show`: drift that no other read reports.

tags.name: Wireless / Devices
tags.description: Wifi radios (`config wifi-device`): band, channel, htmode, country, txpower.

tags.name: Wireless / Interfaces
tags.description: SSIDs (`config wifi-iface`). `key`, `r0kh` and `r1kh` are write-only, and runtime carries iwinfo state.

tags.name: Dhcp / Hosts
tags.description: Static DHCP leases (`config host`).

tags.name: Dhcp / Servers
tags.description: Per-interface DHCP server config (`config dhcp`). runtime carries lease counts.

tags.name: Dhcp / Dnsmasq
tags.description: Global dnsmasq tuning singleton.

tags.name: Dhcp / Odhcpd
tags.description: odhcpd singleton.

tags.name: Dhcp / Leases
tags.description: Leases parsed from /tmp/dhcp.leases (read-only); ?family=v6 returns the odhcpd IPv6 leases instead.

tags.name: System
tags.description: Global system config singleton (`config system`): hostname, timezone, log_size, etc.

tags.name: System / Timeservers
tags.description: NTP server list (`config timeserver`).

tags.name: System / Password
tags.description: Local Unix password (write-only; shells out to passwd).

tags.name: System / SSH authorized keys
tags.description: Manage `/etc/dropbear/authorized_keys` entries by stable id.

tags.name: System / Cron jobs
tags.description: Manage `/etc/crontabs/root` entries by stable id, one per line. Lines from packages, comments and environment lines stay as they are.

tags.name: Dropbear / Instances
tags.description: Per-instance SSH config (`config dropbear`).

tags.name: Uhttpd / Instances
tags.description: Per-instance HTTP server config (`config uhttpd`). The `main` instance keeps uapi's own `ucode_prefix` entry.

tags.name: Uhttpd / Certs
tags.description: px5g certificate generation params (`config cert`).

tags.name: Unbound / Server
tags.description: Recursive DNS server singleton (`config unbound`).

tags.name: Unbound / Srv
tags.description: Directives rendered into unbound's `server:` clause (`config unbound_srv`). Requires the separate `unbound-uci-ext` package, which owns the uci-to-conf renderer and the init script this resource reloads; without it the first write returns `503 init_script_missing`.

tags.name: Unbound / Ext
tags.description: Clauses rendered outside `server:`, such as `forward-zone:` or `view:` (`config unbound_ext`). Same install dependency as Unbound / Srv: `unbound-uci-ext` provides the renderer and the init script, and without it the first write returns `503 init_script_missing`.

tags.name: Sqm / Queues
tags.description: Per-interface SQM shaping (`config queue`).

tags.name: Snmpd / Agents
tags.description: SNMP listen addresses (`config agent`).

tags.name: Snmpd / Com2secs
tags.description: community-to-security mapping (`config com2sec`).

tags.name: Snmpd / Groups
tags.description: SNMP groups (`config group`).

tags.name: Snmpd / Accesses
tags.description: group-to-view ACLs (`config access`).

tags.name: Snmpd / System
tags.description: SNMPv2-MIB system.* singleton (sys_location, sys_contact, etc.).

tags.name: Lldpd / Config
tags.description: LLDP/CDP/etc. toggles singleton.

tags.name: Prometheus Node Exporter Lua / Config
tags.description: node_exporter listen + per-collector toggles singleton.

tags.name: Vnstat / Config
tags.description: Global vnstat singleton.

tags.name: Mwan3 / Globals
tags.description: mwan3 multi-WAN tuning singleton (mark mask, logging, route-monitor interval).

tags.name: Mwan3 / Interfaces
tags.description: Per-WAN tracking config: track_ip probes, failure/recovery thresholds, family.

tags.name: Mwan3 / Members
tags.description: (interface, metric, weight) tuples consumed by policies.

tags.name: Mwan3 / Policies
tags.description: Member groups with a last-resort fallback. Cross-refs `mwan3:members`.

tags.name: Mwan3 / Rules
tags.description: Traffic-match -> policy bindings. Cross-refs `mwan3:policies`.

tags.name: Usteer / Config
tags.description: Passive band-steering daemon singleton (signal thresholds, roam scan intervals, SSID filter).

tags.name: Openvpn / Instances
tags.description: Per-tunnel OpenVPN config. Filesystem paths for ca/cert/dh; key/tls_auth/pkcs12 are write-only (reads return has_<field>).

tags.name: Raw / Generic uci passthrough
tags.description: Escape hatch for any uci section type uapi does not curate. Same atomic-transaction recipe, same auth model. Stable URL/verb/error contract; payload follows uci's moving target.

tags.name: Packages / Installed
tags.description: Manage on-router apk packages (shells out to `apk add`/`del`).

tags.name: Packages / Feeds
tags.description: Manage `/etc/apk/repositories.d/*.list` feed files.

tags.name: Auth / Whoami
tags.description: Token introspection: read the calling bearer's own metadata.

tags.name: Auth / Tokens
tags.description: HTTP token rotation: list, mint, revoke. Mint enforces scope-subset (caller must hold every requested scope).

tags.name: Operational / Healthz
tags.description: Liveness + subsystem checks. No auth. Treat `version` as the stable version-skew probe.

tags.name: Operational / OpenAPI spec
tags.description: Self-describing endpoint serving this OpenAPI document. No auth.

tags.name: Operational / Schema discovery
tags.description: Per-resource schema_properties for dynamic clients without parsing the full spec. No auth.

tags.name: Operational / Metrics
tags.description: Prometheus 0.0.4 text. Path-template labels normalize concrete ids.

tags.name: Operational / Diagnostics
tags.description: Lock state, uptime, loaded resources.

tags.name: Operational / Services
tags.description: Start again a service that procd gave up on.

tags.name: Operational / Batch
tags.description: Multi-package atomic transaction (max 50 ops). 207 Multi-Status on success.

post.summary: Stop and start a service once when procd gave up on one of its instances
post.description:
procd gives up on an instance that dies too often soon after a start, and does not start it again until the next reload or start of its service. `GET /uapi/diagnostics` lists such an instance under `stopped_instances`, and a write after which one stays down answers `X-Reload-Status: stopped`. This action runs what such a write runs once, on request.

`{name}` takes the services that uapi reloads and whose init script sets `respawn` on every instance that it starts. Another name answers 404 `not_found`, whatever the scopes of the token. `network`, `uhttpd` and `dropbear` are not in the list, because the stop acts on the whole service: a stop of `network` or `uhttpd` cuts off the request, and a stop of `dropbear` stops the instance that serves the management SSH session, so a start that fails leaves the router without SSH.

Scope: `uapi:services:rw`, or `rw` on a domain whose writes reload the service, as `dhcp:rw` for `dnsmasq`. The domains of each service: `dnsmasq` (`dhcp:rw`, `system:rw`), `lldpd` (`lldpd:rw`), `mwan3` (`mwan3:rw`), `odhcpd` (`dhcp:rw`, `network:rw`, `system:rw`), `prometheus-node-exporter-lua` (`prometheus_node_exporter_lua:rw`), `snmpd` (`snmpd:rw`), `sysntpd` (`system:rw`), `unbound` (`dhcp:rw`, `system:rw`, `unbound:rw`), `vnstat` (`vnstat:rw`). `*:rw` and `uapi:rw` pass too.

When procd gave up on no instance of the service, uapi stops and starts nothing and answers 200 with an empty `recovered`, also for a service that runs, that the operator stopped, or that the router lacks. Otherwise uapi runs `/etc/init.d/{name} stop`, waits until procd lists no instance of the service, and runs `/etc/init.d/{name} start`, with bounds of 3 s, 2 s and 5 s. The stop and the start act on the whole service, so every instance of it stops and starts again, the ones that ran included, such as the other dnsmasq instances. A start sends no SIGHUP, and procd counts the deaths of each new instance from zero. The steps take their time from `reload_budget_s`, and when it is below 10 s, uapi skips them and answers 500 `recover_failed`. A stop still running after 3 s gets no start.

The request holds the global lock shared and the lock of each package whose writes reload the service, so it answers 423 `locked` while such a write runs. Such a write, and a non-uci write, answers 423 while the request runs, 10 s at most.

200 when every instance that procd had given up on runs after the start: `recovered` names them. 500 `recover_failed` when one is still down: `stopped` names each one, and the message says why. A 200 with an `Idempotency-Key` replays for 24 h.

input.description: Unset, fw4 applies DROP, here and in each firewall/zones section without its own `input`.

output_policy.description: Renamed on the wire from uci's `output` (HCL block keyword). Unset, fw4 applies DROP, here and in each firewall/zones section without its own `output_policy`.

forward.description: Unset, fw4 applies DROP, here and in each firewall/zones section without its own `forward`.

syn_flood.description: Enable SYN flood protection. fw4 applies `synflood_protect`, which LuCI writes, and `syn_flood` only when uci holds no `synflood_protect`, and a read gives the value that fw4 applies. A write of true stores `synflood_protect` 1 and removes `syn_flood`, as LuCI does. A write of false removes `synflood_protect` and stores `syn_flood` 0, where LuCI removes both. A null removes both. A stored list, or a value other than 1, on, true, yes, 0, off, false or no, in either option reads null and is an error of the section: fw4 stops while it reads the defaults and applies no ruleset. A write of the field replaces such a value.

drop_invalid.description: Drop packets with invalid conntrack state. A stored list, or a value other than 1, on, true, yes, 0, off, false or no, reads null and is an error of the section: fw4 stops while it reads the defaults and applies no ruleset. A write of the field replaces such a value, and a null removes it.

synflood_burst.description: Packets above `synflood_rate` that `syn_flood` lets through in a burst. A read gives the number as fw4 parses it, so `0x10` reads 16. Unset, fw4 applies 50. A stored list, or a value that is no number to fw4, such as `abc`, reads null and is an error of the section: fw4 stops while it reads the defaults and applies no ruleset. A number that is no integer, such as `16.5`, reads null and is an error too: nft refuses it, so fw4 applies no ruleset while `syn_flood` is on.

synflood_rate.description: SYN packets that `syn_flood` lets through, as a rate with its unit, such as `25/second`. A read gives it as fw4 applies it, so a stored `25` and `25/s` read `25/second`. A write takes a string only with the whole unit, such as `25/minute`, and refuses `25/m` and the string `"25"`. It also takes an integer, a rate per second. Unset, fw4 applies 25/second. The kernel refuses a limit whose rate plus burst overflows 64 bits, or a slow rate with a large burst, such as `1/minute` with a burst of 4294967295, whose nanoseconds per packet times the burst overflow 64 bits. Such a rate answers 422 `out_of_range`, and a stored one is an error of the section, since fw4 then applies no ruleset while `syn_flood` is on. A stored list, or a value that fw4 refuses, such as `abc`, reads null and is an error of the section: fw4 stops while it reads the defaults and applies no ruleset.

A write of the field replaces such a value, and a null removes it.

NetworkInterfacesResponse.description: uapi resource backed by uci network.interface

id.description: Create-time only; picks the uci section name (which becomes the uapi `id` field). When omitted, the server emits a 14-char `wg_<rand>` for proto=wireguard (fits Linux IFNAMSIZ for the kernel netdev), a 15-char `vpn_<rand>` for proto=openvpn, or a 28-char ULID otherwise. Useful for LuCI parity (`lan`, `wan`, `guest`) and readable cross-references. For proto=wireguard the value must additionally fit IFNAMSIZ (15 chars max). The pattern applies to the create only: a section that LuCI or a shell named otherwise, such as `4g`, takes every other write.

device.description: Physical or logical L2 device this interface binds to

proto.description: Interface protocol. Several values need a handler package on the device: wwan needs `wwan`, wireguard needs `wireguard-tools`, dhcpv6 needs `odhcp6c`, ppp/pppoe need `ppp`, and openvpn needs `openvpn-openssl`, or its `openvpn-mbedtls` or `openvpn-wolfssl` variant. When the handler is missing, the write still succeeds, the interface is inert, and `runtime.effective_proto` reads `none`. netifd loads its handlers when it starts, so a handler package installed later takes effect after a reboot or `/etc/init.d/network restart`. A read answers any proto that uci stores, such as the `6in4` that LuCI writes or the `qmi` that an LTE router ships, while a write takes only the protos that the request schema lists. Another proto is no error of the section: a PATCH that leaves `proto` out passes and keeps the options that its handler reads, and the validation sweep does not list it. A write that leaves a wireguard interface enabled keeps its commit while an enabled `network/wireguard_peers` of the interface holds a value that makes wg refuse the whole interface, and answers `X-Kernel-Status: blocked` with `X-Kernel-Blocked`, which names each such peer.

dns.description: DNS servers that netifd sets for this interface. On proto openvpn too, this is netifd's list and not openvpn's own `--dns`, which uapi does not model: a write stores a uci list, which the openvpn handler does not take for its `dns` option.

ip6assign.description: Prefix length to assign downstream from a delegated prefix

ip6hint.description: Hexadecimal subnet id that picks which part of a delegated or ULA prefix this interface gets, such as `1` or `0x1f`, below `0xffffffff`. netifd uses it only when `ip6assign` is set, from 33 to 64.

ip6ifaceid.description: Interface id of the address this interface takes from an assigned prefix: `eui64`, `random`, or a fixed id whose network half is zero, such as `::1`. On proto dhcpv6, odhcp6c also uses it for the upstream address.

ip6class.description: Prefix classes this interface may take its assignment from: `local` for the ULA prefix, or the name of the interface that received the prefix. Unset means any.

ip6weight.description: Assignment preference: when several interfaces share a prefix, the ones with a higher weight get their subnet first.

mtu.description: MTU that netifd applies to the interface's devices, from 68 up: the device named by `device` when it has no `config device` section of its own (a dotted VLAN such as `br-lan.10` included), and every device that joins the interface later, such as a Wi-Fi netdev, which then lowers a bridge it joins. A device with its own section keeps its own settings: set its MTU on network/devices, after adopting an anonymous section. On ppp and pppoe the value also goes to pppd, which takes 128 to 16384. The wireguard handler applies it to the tunnel itself. A stored value outside these ranges reads as it is, and a write outside them answers 422.

auto.description: Bring this interface up at boot

disabled.description: Whether netifd ignores this interface entirely. A disabled interface is not registered at all, so it has no ubus object and its addresses and routes are not installed. A stored `1` or `true` reads true, as netifd reads it, and any other value reads false. A write stores `1` or `0`. A write that enables a wireguard interface while one of its enabled peers holds a value that makes wg refuse the whole interface keeps its commit, and answers `X-Kernel-Status: blocked`.

ip4table.description: Routing table for the IPv4 routes this interface installs: a number or a name from /etc/iproute2/rt_tables

ip6table.description: Routing table for the IPv6 routes this interface installs: a number or a name from /etc/iproute2/rt_tables

metric.description: Metric of the routes this interface installs without one of their own

defaultroute.description: Install the default route the protocol provides. Unset means true. On openvpn, openvpn-hotplug provides one each time openvpn knows a route gateway, which a `topology subnet` server always pushes, also without `redirect-gateway`. netifd then replaces the default route of wan, and when the tunnel goes down the main table keeps no IPv4 default route until wan restarts. Set false on a client that must not carry the default route.

delegate.description: Hand this interface's IPv6 prefixes on to downstream interfaces. Unset means true.

runtime.description: Populated from ubus network.interface.<name> status; empty {} when the interface has no runtime state.

effective_proto.description: The protocol netifd is actually running for this interface. Differs from the configured `proto` when no handler is registered for it, in which case netifd reports `none` and the interface is inert; a mismatch means the device needs the handler package and a networking restart.

l3_device.description: Kernel device that carries the layer 3 traffic of the interface, such as `pppoe-wan`

ipaddr.description: First entry of the uci `list ipaddr`. Read-only: send `ipaddrs` to write, which names the same uci option.

ipaddrs.description: Full IPv4 address list for static proto (uci `list ipaddr`). The only write name for this option; `ipaddr` is the read-only first entry. On a proto that uapi does not model, such as 6in4, one value is stored as an option, as LuCI writes it, and a write refuses several when the handler reads the option as one value, as netifd publishes it in `get_proto_handlers`: netifd hands such a handler no uci list.

ip6addrs.description: IPv6 address list for static proto (uci `list ip6addr`). A static interface needs either this or `ipaddrs`, not both. On a proto that uapi does not model, such as 6in4, one value is stored as an option, as LuCI writes it, and a write refuses several when the handler reads the option as one value, as netifd publishes it in `get_proto_handlers`: netifd hands such a handler no uci list.

broadcast.description: IPv4 broadcast address (static proto). On proto dhcp the same uci option is a flag, `broadcast_flag`.

ip6gw.description: IPv6 default gateway, a bare address with no prefix length (static proto)

ip6prefix.description: IPv6 prefixes routed to this device for delegation to clients (static, dhcpv6, wireguard). Always an array in both directions. On a proto that uapi does not model, such as 6in4, one value is stored as an option, as LuCI writes it, and a write refuses several when the handler reads the option as one value, as netifd publishes it in `get_proto_handlers`: netifd hands such a handler no uci list.

addresses.description: Proto wireguard requires at least one address, as an IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR.

private_key.description: WireGuard private key; accepted on write, masked on read. A PATCH or PUT that switches the interface to another proto removes it.

listen_port.description: WireGuard listen port. 0 or unset lets the kernel pick one. netifd parses no listen_port, and the proto handler gives wg the number that ucode's int() reads from the stored value, so `0x10` reads 0 and `010` reads 10. A service name that uci stores, such as `openvpn`, reads null: the handler gives wg no port for it, and wg listens on a port that the kernel picks. A PUT of the read removes the name, with no change for wg. -1 reads for a stored number outside 0 to 65535, for which wg refuses the config of the whole interface, so the interface does not come up. A write answers 422 while the interface holds -1. A PATCH that switches to wireguard and does not send a port also answers 422 while uci holds such a number, which the read of the old proto does not show: send a port, or switch with a PUT, which removes it.

nohostroute.description: Suppress the host route that wireguard adds to a peer endpoint and openvpn to its remote server. Only a stored `1` reads true, which is the value that openvpn-hotplug compares it with.

peerdns.description: Use the DNS servers the upstream advertises (dhcp, dhcpv6, pppoe, ppp, wwan, openvpn). On openvpn they are the DNS servers of a pushed `dhcp-option`. Unset means true.

id.description: Create-time only; picks the uci section name (which becomes the uapi `id` field). When omitted, the server emits a 14-char `wg_<rand>` for proto=wireguard (fits Linux IFNAMSIZ for the kernel netdev), a 15-char `vpn_<rand>` for proto=openvpn, or a 28-char ULID otherwise. Useful for LuCI parity (`lan`, `wan`, `guest`) and readable cross-references. For proto=wireguard the value must additionally fit IFNAMSIZ (15 chars max). The pattern applies to the create only: a section that LuCI or a shell named otherwise, such as `4g`, takes every other write.

device.description: Physical or logical L2 device this interface binds to

proto.description: Interface protocol. Several values need a handler package on the device: wwan needs `wwan`, wireguard needs `wireguard-tools`, dhcpv6 needs `odhcp6c`, ppp/pppoe need `ppp`, and openvpn needs `openvpn-openssl`, or its `openvpn-mbedtls` or `openvpn-wolfssl` variant. When the handler is missing, the write still succeeds, the interface is inert, and `runtime.effective_proto` reads `none`. netifd loads its handlers when it starts, so a handler package installed later takes effect after a reboot or `/etc/init.d/network restart`. A read answers any proto that uci stores, such as the `6in4` that LuCI writes or the `qmi` that an LTE router ships, while a write takes only the protos that the request schema lists. Another proto is no error of the section: a PATCH that leaves `proto` out passes and keeps the options that its handler reads, and the validation sweep does not list it. A write that leaves a wireguard interface enabled keeps its commit while an enabled `network/wireguard_peers` of the interface holds a value that makes wg refuse the whole interface, and answers `X-Kernel-Status: blocked` with `X-Kernel-Blocked`, which names each such peer.

dns.description: DNS servers that netifd sets for this interface. On proto openvpn too, this is netifd's list and not openvpn's own `--dns`, which uapi does not model: a write stores a uci list, which the openvpn handler does not take for its `dns` option.

ip6assign.description: Prefix length to assign downstream from a delegated prefix

ip6hint.description: Hexadecimal subnet id that picks which part of a delegated or ULA prefix this interface gets, such as `1` or `0x1f`, below `0xffffffff`. netifd uses it only when `ip6assign` is set, from 33 to 64.

ip6ifaceid.description: Interface id of the address this interface takes from an assigned prefix: `eui64`, `random`, or a fixed id whose network half is zero, such as `::1`. On proto dhcpv6, odhcp6c also uses it for the upstream address.

ip6class.description: Prefix classes this interface may take its assignment from: `local` for the ULA prefix, or the name of the interface that received the prefix. Unset means any.

ip6weight.description: Assignment preference: when several interfaces share a prefix, the ones with a higher weight get their subnet first.

mtu.description: MTU that netifd applies to the interface's devices, from 68 up: the device named by `device` when it has no `config device` section of its own (a dotted VLAN such as `br-lan.10` included), and every device that joins the interface later, such as a Wi-Fi netdev, which then lowers a bridge it joins. A device with its own section keeps its own settings: set its MTU on network/devices, after adopting an anonymous section. On ppp and pppoe the value also goes to pppd, which takes 128 to 16384. The wireguard handler applies it to the tunnel itself. A stored value outside these ranges reads as it is, and a write outside them answers 422.

auto.description: Bring this interface up at boot

disabled.description: Whether netifd ignores this interface entirely. A disabled interface is not registered at all, so it has no ubus object and its addresses and routes are not installed. A write that enables a wireguard interface while one of its enabled peers holds a value that makes wg refuse the whole interface keeps its commit, and answers `X-Kernel-Status: blocked`.

metric.description: Metric of the routes this interface installs without one of their own

id.description: Optional at create: caller-supplied uci section name; becomes the response `id`. When omitted, the server emits a ULID. Read-only after create (rename via DELETE + POST). Charset and length follow uci section-name rules: 1 to 32 characters, start with a letter, alphanumerics and underscore only. Per-resource modules may tighten further (e.g. proto=wireguard interfaces are IFNAMSIZ-tight at 15 chars).

interface.description: Parent WireGuard interface (network/interfaces name with proto=wireguard)

public_key.description: WireGuard public key of the peer, as wg pubkey prints it

allowed_ips.description: IPv4 or IPv6 addresses or CIDRs routed to this peer; a bare address means a single host. A read gives the entries as wg gets them: the proto handler takes a list as its entries and an option as its words, joins them with commas and expands no escape, and wg cuts the line at `#` and splits it at commas. So a comma separates two entries, and a list entry that holds a space or a backslash reads as one entry, which wg refuses, so the interface does not come up. A value that wg reads as nothing, such as one that starts with `#`, reads as one empty entry. With `route_allowed_ips`, the handler routes each entry as stored, past a `#` too, with the length that ucode's int() reads, its leading decimal digits, so `10.0.0.0/0x10` routes 0.0.0.0/0. Each entry that a write leaves must be an address or CIDR, on a disabled peer too. A stored entry that starts with `+` or `-` marks an incremental update to wg, which adds the prefixes of the whole list to what the peer already holds instead of replacing them, and refuses the command for one marked `-`, in `wg set` as in the `wg syncconf` of an ifup. A write refuses such an entry, because it is not an address or CIDR, and the kernel apply and the restore refuse a peer that stores one.

endpoint_host.description: Remote endpoint host name or IP address. An IPv6 address goes without brackets, because the proto handler brackets every host with a colon itself. A write refuses a host with a backslash, a newline, a `#`, or a colon outside an IPv6 address, which can end in a %zone, on a disabled peer too. The handler gives wg an IPv6 address as it stands, and musl's getaddrinfo takes a zone of digits up to 4294967295 on any address, and the name of an interface only on a link-local or multicast link-local address. wg refuses the config of the whole interface for any other zone. A write refuses such a zone with `invalid_format`, on a disabled peer and for a stored host too. A write that sends a zone that names no interface of the router, for an enabled peer with a key, answers 422 `conflict`. The handler gives wg a host of only digits and dots as it stands, so a write refuses one that inet_aton does not read, such as `10.0.0.256`, with `invalid_format`, on a disabled peer and for a stored host too, because wg then refuses the config of the whole interface. The handler looks up every other host with nslookup, a hex address too, leaves out the endpoint of one for which nslookup prints no address, and keeps the peer, so the write sets the peer without it and answers `X-Kernel-Status: omitted`. Apart from the `invalid_format` rules, a stored host is not checked, since a name or an interface can exist at one time and not at another.

endpoint_port.description: Endpoint UDP port. A service name that uci stores, such as `https`, reads as its port from /etc/services, as the proto handler resolves it. 0 reads for a value that the handler cannot read, such as a name that does not resolve, and the handler then leaves the endpoint out. A write answers 422 while the port reads 0, on a disabled peer too. A peer with a host and no port reads null, and the handler gives wg port 51820 for it, as the kernel apply and the restore do. An empty value, which only a hand edit stores, reads null too, and the handler leaves the endpoint out for it, as the kernel apply does.

persistent_keepalive.description: Seconds between keepalive packets. 0, a stored `off` or no value turns them off. -1 reads for a stored value that the proto handler cannot read, and the handler then leaves the keepalive out. A write answers 422 while the keepalive reads -1, on a disabled peer too.

route_allowed_ips.description: Auto-install routes for allowed_ips. A stored value other than `1` reads false, as the proto handler reads it.

disabled.description: Skip this peer when starting the tunnel. A stored value other than `1` reads false, as the proto handler reads it.

runtime.description: What the kernel holds for the peer, read-only. It is never part of the desired state or of a plan diff: it shows what the kernel holds beside the fields that uci holds, so that a client can report the difference, which a peer that `wg` changed by hand or a failed apply leaves. uapi compares nothing and corrects nothing. A GET reads it with one `wg show <interface> dump` for each interface of the peers that it reads. A write answers {} and reads no kernel state: read in a write, it would come from before the kernel apply, and `X-Kernel-Status` says whether the apply landed. A GET in a `/uapi/batch` that writes answers {} too, since it runs before the apply of the batch. Also {} when uapi did not read the kernel, because netifd does not report the interface up, wg fails, or wg prints a dump in a shape that uapi does not read, so that a failed read never looks like a missing peer.

in_kernel.description: The kernel holds a peer under the stored `public_key`, which the proto handler gives wg as it is. false for a stored value that is not a key. The other fields are null when this is false. Two peers of an interface that store the same key share the one peer of the kernel, and both report it, a disabled one included.

endpoint.description: The endpoint of the peer in the kernel, as an address and a port, such as `192.0.2.1:51820` or `[2001:db8::1]:51820`. wg resolves a host name when it sets the peer, and the kernel moves the endpoint to the address that an authenticated packet of the peer comes from, so this can differ from `endpoint_host` and `endpoint_port` with no write: a peer without `endpoint_host` reads the address that it last sent from. null when the kernel holds no endpoint for the peer.

allowed_ips.description: The allowed IPs of the peer in the kernel, in the form that the kernel prints: an address and a prefix length, with the host bits cleared and an IPv6 address in its short lower-case form, so a stored `10.0.0.2` reads `10.0.0.2/32`, `10.0.0.5/24` reads `10.0.0.0/24` and `FD00:0::1/64` reads `fd00::/64`. A write takes host bits and any IPv6 spelling, so a client compares the two in that form. Empty when the kernel holds none for the peer.

persistent_keepalive.description: The keepalive interval of the peer in the kernel, in seconds, 0 when it is off.

latest_handshake.description: The time of the latest handshake with the peer, in seconds since the epoch, 0 when there was none.

rx_bytes.description: Bytes that the kernel received from the peer since it added the peer.

tx_bytes.description: Bytes that the kernel sent to the peer since it added the peer.

preshared_key.description: Optional preshared key, as wg genpsk prints it. A write sets it, and a read does not show it. A null, or a write that leaves it out, keeps the stored key. To remove it, create the peer again without it, or remove the option through /raw.

device.description: Radios (wireless/devices ids) of this SSID. netifd sets the SSID up on each radio that the option names, as a list or as words split at any whitespace, and a read gives these radios as an array. A write takes a string of words or a list, and stores one radio as a string, as LuCI and `wifi config` write it

network.description: Network interfaces this SSID bridges into. netifd attaches the SSID to each network that the option names, as a list or as words split at any whitespace, and a read gives these networks as an array. A write takes a string of words or a list, and stores one network as a string, as LuCI writes it

mode.description: A section without a mode reads null: wifi-scripts sets up nothing for it. A null on write removes the option. A write refuses mode wds, for which wifi-scripts sets up no interface; LuCI writes a WDS access point or station as mode ap or sta with option wds. A read reports a stored wds or ahdemo, which wifi-scripts skips as it skips a section without a mode, and which is no error.

ssid.description: SSID broadcast (or joined in sta mode). A write refuses more than 32 bytes, which hostapd and wpa_supplicant refuse in mode ap, sta and adhoc. uapi counts bytes, so a non-ASCII character counts for more than one. In mode monitor, adhoc or mesh, it must not hold a single quote. wifi-scripts gives the daemon a list that uci holds as the JSON text of the list, such as `[ "home", "net" ]`, and a read gives that text

A write refuses wep with `conflict` unless the router sets WEP up. isolate.description: Block station-to-station traffic on this AP

ieee80211r.description: 802.11r fast BSS transition between the access points of one mobility domain

ft_over_ds.description: 802.11r over the distribution system instead of over the air

ft_psk_generate_local.description: Generate the 802.11r keys locally instead of using the R0/R1 key holders. Unset, hostapd uses the BSSID without colons. A read gives the number that wifi-scripts reads from the stored text: ` 500` is 500, `0x10` is 16, a fraction is cut, and other text is 0, as hostapd reads it. wifi-scripts stops the setup of the radio, with all its SSIDs, for a value outside the range on an enabled SSID in mode ap, sta, adhoc or mesh. A write refuses such a value also on a disabled SSID or in another mode

r0_key_lifetime.description: 802.11r lifetime of the PMK-R0 in minutes, 0 or more. Unset, hostapd uses 14 days (20160 minutes). 0 turns the timeout off. A read gives the number that wifi-scripts reads from the stored text, as for reassociation_deadline

r1_key_holder.description: 802.11r R1 key holder id, 12 hex digits. Unset, hostapd derives it from the BSSID. hostapd refuses its whole config for another form, which a write refuses also where hostapd does not read it. wifi-scripts writes a list that uci holds as its entries joined by spaces, and a read gives that text

pmk_r1_push.description: Push the PMK-R1 to the other key holders instead of waiting for them to pull it

has_r0kh.description: True if r0kh is configured (the entries are never returned)

has_r1kh.description: True if r1kh is configured (the entries are never returned)

runtime.description: Populated from ubus iwinfo info/assoclist for the runtime interface that backs this uci section; empty {} when the iface has not been provisioned yet.

has_key.description: True if a key is configured (cleartext never returned)

key.description: Encryption passphrase; accepted on write, masked on read. A null, or a write that leaves it out, keeps the stored key, and an empty string removes it, unless the encryption needs a key. Required for every encryption other than none, wep and owe when no key is stored yet, which validate() enforces. A stored EAP SSID without a key, as LuCI writes it, is no error, and a write that changes the encryption to an EAP mode needs one. In mode sta or adhoc, other than with plain sae, the key must be 8 to 63 bytes with no control character, because wifi-scripts gives wpa_supplicant every key as a passphrase, a key of 64 hex digits too. In mode sta, adhoc or mesh, the key must not hold a `#` after an odd number of double quotes. uapi counts bytes. A write answers 422 while the stored key holds such a problem, also on a disabled SSID

r0kh.description: 802.11r R0 key holders as `<MAC>,<NAS id>,<key>` entries, accepted on write, masked on read. A null, or a write that leaves it out, keeps the stored entries, and an empty list removes them. An entry takes no newline and at most 1024 bytes, and while hostapd reads the lists, the form that hostapd parses. Unset with ft_psk_generate_local off, wifi-scripts derives one entry from the mobility domain and the key

r1kh.description: 802.11r R1 key holders as `<MAC>,<R1KH id>,<key>` entries, accepted on write, masked on read. A null, or a write that leaves it out, keeps the stored entries, and an empty list removes them. An entry takes no newline and at most 1024 bytes, and while hostapd reads the lists, the form that hostapd parses

id.description: Optional at create: caller-supplied uci section name; becomes the response `id`. When omitted, the server emits a ULID. Read-only after create (rename via DELETE + POST). Charset and length follow uci section-name rules: 1 to 32 characters, start with a letter, alphanumerics and underscore only. name.description: Hostname dnsmasq answers for this reservation. A comma, a double quote, a `#` or a control character is refused, because the name goes into dnsmasq's config line.

macs.description: MAC addresses for this reservation, the whole uci `list mac`. dnsmasq.init splits the entries into words, and a read gives those words. An octet can be `*`, which dnsmasq matches against any value, as in `00:11:22:33:44:*`. odhcpd skips the whole host when it cannot parse one of its MACs, as it cannot parse one with `*`, so it then gives this host no lease, not even for its duid.

tag.description: dnsmasq tags set on a request this reservation matches, for other options to match on (LuCI's Set Tag). dnsmasq.init joins a list with spaces and splits the tags into words, and a read gives those words, so a stored `option tag 'a b'` and a list entry `a b` both read as two tags. A comma, a double quote, a `#` or a control character is refused.

match_tag.description: dnsmasq tags a request must carry for this reservation to apply (LuCI's Match Tag), the uci `list match_tag`; `!` negates. Only a tag dnsmasq sets from the request before it looks up hosts can match, such as one from a `config vendorclass`, `config userclass` or `config mac` rule. `known` and the DHCP range's own tag are set later, so `known` never matches and `!known` always does (measured on dnsmasq 2.93). A scalar `option match_tag` reads as null, because dnsmasq ignores it. A comma, a double quote, a `#`, a control character or a blank value is refused.

dns.description: Answer DNS queries for this reservation's hostname

broadcast.description: Force broadcast replies for clients that need it

instance.description: Pin this reservation to a specific dhcp/dnsmasq instance (section name)

expires_at.description: Unix epoch seconds when the lease expires, null for a lease that does not expire. dnsmasq writes 0 for such a v4 lease, and odhcpd gives 0xffffffff for such a v6 lease

iaid.description: Identity association id, in hex (v6 entries only)

interface.description: Network device that odhcpd served the lease on, such as `br-lan`, not the uci interface (v6 entries only)

ia_type.description: An address (`IA_NA`) or a delegated prefix (`IA_PD`) (v6 entries only)

prefix_length.description: Length of a delegated prefix; null for an address (v6 entries only)

hostname.description: Client hostname, null when the client sent none. A v6 entry gives the bytes that the client sent, as odhcpd holds them, which are not always a valid DNS name. A stored name or number that iptables refuses reads as it is, and mwan3 then loads none of its rules. mwan3 matches `src_port` and `dest_port` only for tcp or udp in lower case, and drops them for any other proto, such as TCP, 6 or all. With a port, a write refuses tcp or udp in another case, such as TCP, and a stored one blocks every write of the section. A port with another proto is no error.

RequestId.description: Equivalent to the `X-Request-Id` header, which wins when it matches the pattern. The response echoes the value in `X-Request-Id`, and the log lines of the request carry it. When neither form matches the pattern, the request gets a new ULID.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds the client should wait before retrying (RFC 7231 6.6.4)

ETag.description: Quoted hash of the resource body (minus volatile `runtime` state). Stable across unchanged sibling sections; mutates only when the resource itself changes. Use with `If-Match` (or `?if_match=`) on writes for optimistic concurrency.

XRequestId.description: The `X-Request-Id` header of the request when it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,128}$`, else `?request_id=` when it matches, else a new ULID.

Link.description: RFC 8288 link relations; rel="next" present when more paginated items exist.

XKernelUnread.description: Comma-separated up interfaces with proto=wireguard whose kernel peers uapi could not read, because `wg show <interface> dump` failed or printed a shape that uapi does not read. The list holds no entry for them, so an absent header is what says that the list covers every up interface.

XNextCursor.description: Convenience companion to Link rel=next: the bare next-cursor token.

IdempotentReplayed.description: Set to true when a POST response was served from the Idempotency-Key cache instead of being re-applied.

XReloadStatus.description: Outcome of the post-commit daemon reload. `ok` = init script exited 0 (NOT a runtime-convergence promise, see docs/operations.md). `no_reload` = no init script ran, because the write changed nothing in uci, such as a PATCH that names no field, or a PUT or a PATCH that sends the values that uci holds, or because procd runs none of the daemons that read the write. Only a `dhcp` write meets the second case: dnsmasq, odhcpd and unbound are each reloaded only while procd runs them. `unverified` = the write keeps its commit, and whether its daemons take the new config is unknown. Either an init script was still running when uapi stopped waiting for the reloads of the request, 20 s after the first started, and uapi did not kill it, so it and the reloads after it run on. Or every init script exited 0, but the `dnsmasq --test` check that follows a dhcp write did not finish: it was killed after 10 s, or by another SIGKILL. `stopped` = the write keeps its commit, but a daemon that it reloaded is down, and procd will not start it again on its own. `X-Reload-Stopped` names each such instance. Only dnsmasq meets it today: the SIGHUP that the reload of dnsmasq.init sends right after procd restarts an instance can kill the new dnsmasq, and procd gives up on an instance at its sixth such death in a row, because a reload does not reset the count. uapi then stops and starts dnsmasq once, which sends no SIGHUP and starts the instance with a count of zero, and answers `ok` when dnsmasq runs again. The stop and the start take their time from what is left of `reload_budget_s`, and uapi skips them when less than 10 s are left. `unverified` wins over `stopped`: when the start of dnsmasq has not ended within its 5 s, or another check did not finish, the value is `unverified`, and `X-Reload-Stopped` comes beside it when the check found an instance down. The recovery is `POST /uapi/services/dnsmasq/recover`, which stops and starts dnsmasq once more. `service dnsmasq restart` on the router and a write that changes the dhcp config start it too. `GET /uapi/diagnostics` lists such an instance under `stopped_instances` until then. Present on curated-resource writes and the `POST /uapi/batch` 207, where it covers the services of the packages that the batch changed. A `system/cron_jobs` write answers it alone, as `unverified`, when its reload of cron was still running, and syslog then holds the note. Raw passthrough and the other non-uci writes return no reload headers.

XReloadServices.description: Comma-separated list of init scripts that were reloaded after the write committed, in the order in which they ran. With `unverified`, one of them can still be running, and those after it run when it ends, unless it fails. A daemon that reads the config but that the router can lack, or that the operator stopped, is reloaded and listed only while procd runs it: a `dhcp/servers` or `dhcp/hosts` write answers `dnsmasq,odhcpd,unbound`, and leaves out each of them that does not run. A `system` write answers `system,log,dnsmasq,odhcpd,unbound`, and a `network` write `network,odhcpd`, in the same way. The `POST /uapi/batch` 207 lists its services sorted. Present when X-Reload-Status is `ok`, `unverified` or `stopped`, absent when it is `no_reload`, and absent wherever X-Reload-Status itself is.

XReloadStopped.description: Comma-separated list of the procd instances that are down after the write, and that procd will not start again on its own, each as `<service>/<instance>`. Present when X-Reload-Status is `stopped`, and beside `unverified` when the check found an instance down. Absent otherwise.

XKernelStatus.description: Whether the write reached the kernel as well as uci. `ok` = every targeted interface was applied. `partial` = some were applied, and others were skipped or blocked. `skipped` = none was, because the interface is down or netifd does not know it, and uci is still committed and the change takes effect on the next ifup. netifd restarts the interface on each peer change, and uapi waits up to 8 s for that restart. A restart that does not end in time fails a write that sets a peer, with a restore. When the write only removes peers of the interface, by a DELETE or a write that disables them, the interface is skipped instead and the write keeps its commit: the next setup reads uci, which no longer holds them. `blocked` = an enabled `network/wireguard_peers` of a targeted interface holds a value for which wg refuses the config of the whole interface, so the interface does not come up, and the write applied no other interface. X-Kernel-Blocked names each such peer. The write keeps its commit, with no restore. uapi neither waits for the restart of such an interface nor applies the write to it, and netifd sets the peers from uci at the next setup once the peer is fixed, disabled or deleted. A write of `network/interfaces` that leaves a wireguard interface enabled answers `blocked` too, because netifd restarts the interface, and `no_kernel` otherwise. `omitted` = the apply set a peer without the endpoint that uci holds for it, as the proto handler does: the handler leaves out the endpoint of a host that does not resolve, or of a port that it cannot read. A read shows the endpoint that the kernel holds in `runtime.endpoint`, null after the restart of the handler. It takes the place of `ok`, and of `partial` when the write also skipped or blocked an interface: X-Kernel-Applied then names only the interfaces that were applied, so a skipped one is an interface that the write targets and the header does not name. `no_kernel` = the write had nothing for the kernel, because the resource has no kernel path, which is the value on most writes, or the write changed nothing in uci. Absent on raw and non-uci writes, which do not run the kernel apply.

XKernelApplied.description: Comma-separated list of the interfaces whose kernel state was actually changed. Absent when nothing was applied, so also absent whenever X-Kernel-Status is `skipped`, `blocked` or `no_kernel`.

XKernelBlocked.description: Comma-separated list of the `network/wireguard_peers` that keep an interface of the write down, each as `<interface>/<id>`, where `id` is the one that `GET /network/wireguard_peers/{id}` takes, an unmanaged section included. Each is enabled and holds a value for which wg refuses the config of the whole interface, such as an allowed IP that wg cannot parse, or an IPv6 link-local host whose %zone names no interface of the router. A write refuses each such value that it sends. Only another writer, such as LuCI, stores one, or the interface of a zone goes away. `GET /uapi/diagnostics?validate=1` lists each such peer. Present with X-Kernel-Status `blocked`, and beside `partial` or `omitted` when the write also applied another interface. Absent otherwise.

XMgmtPathWarning.description: Advisory: the write reached the path this request arrived through, so the connection carrying it may be about to break. Two shapes. `interface=<name> changed=<fields>` when a `network/interfaces` write moved or removed the interface the request came in on. `device=<name> changed=<fields>` when a `network/bridge_vlans` or `network/devices` write targeted the caller's device, or the bridge that device is a port of: a bridge-vlan enables VLAN filtering for the whole bridge and drops untagged traffic, and a device write can change that bridge's ports. Emitted on create as well as on the three item writes, because a new section can claim the management device. The write already happened and was not refused; severing your own path is a legitimate operation. Absent when the write could not be shown to reach the caller, which includes the case where uapi cannot resolve the inbound device at all.

PreconditionFailed.description: A precondition failed: If-Match did not match the current ETag, If-None-Match matched it (or was `*` against an existing resource), or a JSON-Patch test op failed. Preconditions are evaluated before the transaction runs, so a 412 means nothing was written

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body is over 262144 bytes (256 KiB), its Content-Length is not a whole number from 0 to 262144, or it holds more than 2000 `{` and `[` characters. Checked before the bearer check (code: payload_too_large)

ValidationFailed.description: Request body failed validation (per-field errors in `errors[]`). A write of a uci section is checked as the section that it leaves, so a stored value that breaks a rule fails it too, until a write replaces the value or the change goes through `/raw`.

Locked.description: Another write holds the same per-package lock; retry after Retry-After seconds
